profile.headline: Bioinformatics Engineer III at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
EXPERTISE AND SKILLS:
•	Parallel and cluster computing.
•	NGS data analysis, pipeline design, and implementation.
•	Large-scale data integration and data mining.
•	Transcriptomic data analysis (RNA-Seq, miRNA, etc).
•	Statistical analysis of high throughput data.
•	Programming in many languages including Python, R, Java, C, php, MySQL and shell scripts.
•       Genome assembly and annotation.
•       Machine learning algorithms.
•       Data visualization.
•       Relational database design and management.
•       Unix / Linux administration.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Software Engineer III
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States

positions.title: Senior Programmer Analyst / Bioinformatician
positions.description:
Center for Infection and Immunity.  Perform next generation sequence analysis of large data sets and provide bioinformatics solutions for a variety of projects.  Data mining, visualization, interpretation.  

Responsible for developing and maintaining high-throughput NGS data processing pipelines for use on high-performance computing clusters.

Responsible for all transcriptomic data analysis for the center, including projects focusing on Ebola, MERS-CoV, Influenza, ME/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, Autism, and Crimean Congo Hemorrhagic Fever.

Develop algorithms and perform other data analyses as needed such as serology-based assays to identify discriminatory disease epitopes for diagnostic platforms, integration of multiple data types in Chronic Fatigue studies (epigenetic, proteomic, metagenomic, clinical), and development of machine-learning and statistical approaches for analysis of various data types.

Perform functional analysis and interpretation of host-pathogen response, participate in grant submissions, and write papers for peer-reviewed publication.

positions.title: Ph.D Candidate
positions.description: Worked on a variety of research projects such as full transcriptome RNA secondary structure prediction and it's impact on GC content, data visualization of gene neighborhoods and phylogony, meta-analysis of reference genome reliant analysis methodology, and start-to-finish genome sequencing, assembly, and annotation.

positions.title: Systems Programmer
positions.description: Developed several cross platform programs for use in company call centers and managed several large databases of customer information to ensure proper call rotation and information about related customers, in addition to regularly providing solutions to ad-hoc problems.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: I worked as part of a small team developing various enterprise level applications in Ruby on Rails, such as catalog management and warranty claim tracking applications.  I have also worked in converting older applications from PHP to Ruby on Rails.  Development was done in a multi-platform environment and applications function across multiple databases.  The team has made significant progress toward standardizing company software and developing new applications.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Researched general solutions to technical computing problems; Developed and provided support for distance education platforms; Designed, implemented, and administered multiple web services. Installed and administered Content Management Systems such as Drupal, Sakai, and Moodle. Provided general solutions for varying issues using PHP.

positions.title: English Instructor
positions.description: Developed and implemented strategies for teaching English to children.

honors.title: Lucille P. and Edward C. Giles Dissertation-Year Fellowship
honors.description:
This fellowship was established to recognize and support students who are in the final stages of a Doctoral degree in the STEM disciplines to include Computing and Information Systems, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biology, Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, Applied Mathematics, Optical Science and Engineering, and Nanoscale Science.
Funding for this award was made possible by the generosity of the Edward C. Giles Foundation and Lucille P. Giles.
